learnings.text:
---
title: Overview capacity should use the same current machines as Swarm
author: Jack
date: 2026-11-18
branch: feat/overview-capacity
cost: { minutes: 7, tokens: 49452 }
id: l-2915ce45
scope: repo
status: active
src: agent
touches:
  - src/features/overview/Infrastructure.tsx
  - src/features/overview/capacity.ts
  - src/api/adapters/swarm.ts
---

## Decided

Use the Swarm read for fleet capacity in Overview. The enrollment list includes historical and revoked workers and lacks a reliable shared slot count. Headline availability is installation-wide and uses the server-reported idle count, worker holds, and machine maximum. Show the lowest fresh reading by resource so a fleet average cannot hide one crowded machine.

## Tried and ruled out

Startup credential configuration and the full enrollment list took up the Capacity pane without answering how many more agents could start. Subtracting occupied slots from configured slots can invent open slots when Swarm reports a worker-wide hold.

## Watch out

Idle capacity still depends on project, provider, and worker admission. Keep missing totals and stale or missing telemetry explicit. The current worker machine report has CPU, memory, and disk fields but no GPU reading.

In the code:
`src/features/overview/Infrastructure.tsx` uses GET /api/v1/swarm with the same cache key as Swarm. Capacity view calculations live in `src/features/overview/capacity.ts`.

learnings.text:
---
title: Offer an all-projects exit when a selected project has no playbook library
author: Jack
date: 2026-11-18
branch: fix/playbooks-project-scope
cost: { minutes: 30, tokens: 70437 }
id: l-555318cc
scope: repo
status: active
src: agent
touches:
  - src/features/playbooks/CurrentCatalog.tsx
  - src/features/playbooks/Playbooks.tsx
---

## Decided

When a project-scoped Playbooks collection is unavailable, explain the selected scope and offer a link that removes the project filter while keeping the current Playbooks view. Keep the exact-item error for failed individual lookups.

## Tried and ruled out

The rollout browser probe opened a fresh All projects URL. That passed while project-scoped navigation still showed a generic missing-item message. Silently discarding the project selection would hide the scope change from the user.

## Watch out

The live runtime can serve a single playbook namespace even when the project picker lists several repositories. A project outside that namespace gets a scoped 404 from the collection. Probe both a matching project and a different project when qualifying Playbooks on a real runtime.

In the code: the catalog client classifies failures at response headers and leaves their bodies unread. The scope recovery uses the project filter and HTTP status while preserving routing and authorization.

---
title: Open the compiled workflow first on Playbooks
author: Jack
date: 2026-11-18
branch: feat/playbooks-graph-first
cost: { minutes: 28, tokens: 283419 }
id: l-9218fa77
scope: repo
status: active
src: agent
touches:
  - src/features/playbooks/Playbooks.tsx
  - docs/specs/0002-product-design.md
---

## Decided

The Playbooks landing page should answer what a workflow does. The user prefers the v1 node graph as the starting point. Keep run history one tab away, put version and rollback controls under Deployments, and show request-to-run outcomes under Run history as Start requests.

## Tried and ruled out

The existing Run history timeline describes a particular execution. It cannot show unvisited branches or a playbook that has never run. The current catalog lists artifacts and entry names but does not carry transitions.

## Watch out

Match the immutable artifact digest and namespace. A run's Definition tab must keep showing the workflow for its pinned version even after deployment moves to another version. A missing stored graph should leave the playbook and its metadata available.

In the code: the dashboard reads the owner-scoped install-time projection from `/api/playbooks/inspection/definitions/{artifact}/graph`. The projection is shared with the server's run inspection.

learnings.name: 2026-11-17-keep-saved-agent-history-readable-without-jack.md
learnings.text:
---
title: Use native provider messages for readable agent history
author: Jack
date: 2026-11-17
branch: fix/agents-history-rendering
cost: { minutes: 57, tokens: 237781 }
id: l-866b5b8a
scope: repo
status: active
src: agent
touches:
  - src/features/agents/history/History.tsx
  - src/features/agents/history/compactTranscript.ts
  - src/features/agents/history/History.test.tsx
  - src/app/Shell.test.tsx
  - src/app/Shell.tsx
  - src/app/destinations.ts
  - tests/shell.spec.ts
  - tests/visual/tablet.spec.ts
  - src/api/sessionHistory.ts
---

## Decided

The owner judged the terminal cleanup insufficient because the message text itself remains distorted. Use the providers' native messages as the candidate source for a readable conversation history. Keep PTY output available for terminal-specific diagnostics.

## Tried and ruled out

Filtering border glyphs and whitespace still leaves words joined by cursor motions that were discarded at capture time. The regular Docker context made the sampled sandboxes appear missing. Querying the worker's configured Podman socket confirmed that some stopped manual sandboxes retain native JSONL with both user and assistant text.

## Watch out

An existing sandbox is not proof that it has session messages. Backfill requires the original sandbox and usable provider records. The native observation normalizer emits text references with digests, so it is evidence of schema support rather than a ready-made content archive. Any ingestion should bind the discovered file to the AQ session, parse only the necessary message fields, and avoid sending credential files or raw provider dumps to the dashboard.

In the code:
- Manual provider startup sets the sandbox home in aq-worker's `crates/aq-worker/src/bin/aq-worker/manual/provider.rs`.
- Claude Code's native records were found under `/aq/home/.claude/projects/`; Codex's were under `/aq/home/.codex/sessions/`.
- Existing terminal retention uses `crates/aq-worker/src/bin/aq-worker/manual/recording.rs`. The file-based observation formats are in `crates/aq-observation-engine/src/formats/`.
- The current dashboard reader in `src/features/agents/history/History.tsx` calls the plain-text archive through `src/api/sessionHistory.ts`. The display-only experiment in `src/features/agents/history/compactTranscript.ts` does not address the reported distortion.
